evaluations.label: A
errors: "Management decided against including teletext support or voice recognition" - management only ruled out teletext; voice recognition was set aside by the team in discussion
Attributes "potential LCD screens or sliding hatches" to the technical-functions presenter; the LCD screen came from the Marketing Expert's research and the sliding panel from later group discussion
"Infrared was selected as the preferred method" presented as a decision; it was the Industrial Designer's opinion
Unresolved questions such as "Would adding a 'find my remote' beep function fit within budget?" were never raised in the meeting
"Action Items (none)" - the meeting assigned a questionnaire and summary, individual concept work per role, and the PM uploading minutes and slides
Voice recognition dismissed partly for "potential complexity for the target user" - not a reason given
strengths: Captures key market research numbers (75%, 80%, 10% of buttons)
Covers the four-component working design, the corporate image requirement and the 12.50/25 euro figures
weaknesses: No action items at all despite clear assignments
Generic speaker labels (Speaker 2, 3, 4, 5) make roles hard to follow
Several misattributions and invented open questions
Target group outcome (left open) is muddled

evaluations.label: B
errors: Some timestamps are slightly off (e.g. working design at [15:20], selling point at [14:21]) - minor
strengths: Correctly states the target demographic was left open and lists the ranges floated (15-35, under 65, 20-55) and the spending-ability idea
Accurate on scope (TV only, no teletext), brand requirements, 25 euro retail and 12.50 production cap
Covers the hidden secondary buttons idea including the PM's chip-transmission caveat
Captures post-meeting tasks, individual workstreams, coach emails and the file-sharing issue with the PM's presentation
weaknesses: Formal action item list only names the PM; individual role assignments and questionnaire are not listed as owned actions
Omits the Marketing Expert's offer to email more age data before the next meeting
Owner given as 'Speaker 1' rather than the role

evaluations.label: C
errors: "Target group 15-35 years" presented as settled; the group left the target open and leaned toward broad appeal / under 65
"Investigate technical feasibility for rechargeable battery" as an action item is a stretch; the UI Designer only mused about whether a battery is needed
"Quick market rollout" listed as a requirement - loosely based on PM wanting it out quickly, minor
strengths: Concise and mostly accurate on research figures, infrared preference, four components and the 12.5 euro cost limit
Captures core functional decisions: simplicity and fashion, large buttons, hidden functions, loss prevention, cradle idea
weaknesses: Telegraphic fragments with little context for someone who missed the meeting
Misses questionnaire, summary, individual role assignments, coach instructions, 25 euro retail price, slogan
Action items unassigned and partly speculative

evaluations.label: D
errors: "Working design presentation not yet on the server; save from email into shared folder" - the Industrial Designer said the working design was uploaded; it was the Project Manager's presentation that was missing from the server
"age segmentation less useful than lifestyle/attitude targeting" - the discussion was about income/spending ability and focusing on objectives, not lifestyle/attitude
"Infrared chosen over alternatives" overstates the Industrial Designer's personal recommendation as a decision
strengths: Rich and well organized: research numbers including RSI and 65% channel zapping, LCD idea, sliding panel, branding details (yellow/black, Rs)
Clear list of agreed functions and scope (TV only, no teletext, 25/12.50 euro)
Covers questionnaire, summary, 30 minutes individual work, role workstreams, coach email, and the Marketing Expert's offer to send more age data
weaknesses: Misstates which presentation was missing from the shared folder
Presents some ideas (battery solution) as more settled than they were

rationale: B is the most accurate and correctly conveys what was decided versus left open (target group open, voice recognition disfavored), with timestamps and follow-up items; its main gap is thin owner assignment. D is the most detailed and very useful but misidentifies the presentation missing from the shared folder and slightly reframes the targeting discussion. A has decent content but misattributes the voice recognition decision to management, invents unresolved questions and lists no action items. C is terse, states the 15-35 target group as decided, and omits most follow-up tasks.
